title: Bubble in the Sun: Florida's 1920s boom
text:
Just read Chris Knowlton's Bubble in the Sun: The Florida Boom of the 1920s and How It Brought on the Great Depression (2020).  This is a captivating history of the aggressive development of the east coast of Florida by wealthy industrialists and the go-go culture of the roaring 1920s with a great migration of people to make a buck in real estate. 

The story focuses on 4 men and a woman. Henry Flagler, co-founder of Standard Oil (along with JD Rockefeller) takes his wealth to St Augustine and begins an ambitious second career building mega hotel resorts and importantly the Florida East Coast Railway, which connects the east coast to Miami initially, then extends to the keys!  Other notable characters include Carl Fisher who made his fortune in the auto industry develops the local roads around Miami, George Merrick has a vision for a new city in Coral Gables, and Addison Mizner (along with his dead-beat brother Wilson) who is a creative architect who develops Boca and Palm Beach with massive resort hotels and private residences. Marjorie Stoneman Douglas is the daughter of the editor of Miami Herald, is a writer and environmentalist who focuses on preserving the Everglades (who lives to be 107 and was awarded the Presidential Medal by Obama at age 103).

The story focuses on greed and over exuberance on borrowing, debt-financed real estate deals, insider dealing by hucksters, lack of banking regulations leading to the collapse of Florida banks, preceding the stock market crash of 1929 and the protracted depression. All 4 luminaries reach great heights, before becoming penniless and dying prematurely!  The story is riveting and is probably less well-known than the westward migration, the gold rush (SF or Alaska), or Vegas!  There are elements of excess, greed, corruption, invincibility of the pioneering spirit.
